title: Customer-priority sieve and acceptance criteria for top-account escalation intake
creator: Marta Singh
description:
Goal: Define a deterministic 'sieve' and clear acceptance criteria for inbound requests from strategic/top accounts and escalation channels so Product can make consistent, explainable intake decisions that feed the public roadmap lanes or the high-touch engineering queue.

Background: Over the past 9 months we've onboarded multiple enterprise customers who expect SLA-driven commitments for roadmap items. Sales and Customer Success have escalated requests directly to PMs and Eng. Without a repeatable filter and acceptance criteria we risk over-committing engineering capacity and creating opaque promises to customers. This ticket ships a lightweight decisioning framework (the sieve), a checklist for acceptance, and a small handoff playbook for cases that get rejected or deferred.

Scope:
- Design the sieve: criteria buckets (impact, revenue+renewal risk, security/compliance requirement, integration complexity, time-to-value).
- Define quantitative thresholds where possible (e.g., ARR influence > $500k OR renewal at-risk probability > 30% triggers expedited review).
- Produce a 6-point acceptance checklist for roadmap commit and a 4-point checklist for high-touch engineering queue.
- Specify required artifacts from customer-facing teams (use case doc, business metrics, expected SLO uplift, compliance certs).
- Create fallback paths: canary commitment (pilot), product workaround, or formal backlog deferral with SLA.
- Capture communication templates and PRD/Confluence links for approved and rejected outcomes.

Out-of-scope: building intake UI flows in the Console (separate ticket), large contract negotiation mechanics handled by Sales Ops, and technical implementation work (ENG tickets to follow).
